title: Maximum Increasing Triplet Value
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, consider every triplet of indices `(i, j, k)` with `i < j < k` whose values strictly increase: `nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k]`. The value of such a triplet is `nums[i] - nums[j] + nums[k]`.

Return the largest value over all such triplets. The input is guaranteed to contain at least one strictly increasing triplet.
constraints: nums contains at least one triplet i < j < k with nums[i] < nums[j] < nums[k]
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every triplet is O(n³). Fix the middle index `j` instead: the two outer terms no longer interact. The best `k` is simply the largest value to the right, as long as it beats `nums[j]`. The best `i` is the largest value to the left that is still smaller than `nums[j]`: a predecessor query, which is what an ordered set of the values seen so far answers. JavaScript has no built-in tree set, so a Fenwick tree over the values' ranks plays that role: it stores, for ranges of ranks, the largest value inserted.

## Approach

1. Fill `rightMax[k]`, the largest value from index `k` to the end (`0` past the end).
2. Give each distinct value a `rank` from 1 in sorted order, and create an empty Fenwick `tree`.
3. For each `j` from left to right: `left = largestBelow(r - 1)` is the largest earlier value with a smaller rank, and `right = rightMax[j + 1]`.
4. If `left > 0` (some smaller value exists) and `right > nums[j]`, update `best` with `left - nums[j] + right`.
5. `insert` `nums[j]` so later indices can use it, then return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [5, 6, 9]` and `rightMax = [9, 9, 9, 0]`. At `j = 0` nothing is smaller on the left. At `j = 1`, `left = 5` and `right = 9 > 6`, so `best = 5 - 6 + 9 = 8`. At `j = 2`, `right = 0`, so nothing changes. The answer is `8`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for sorting and one Fenwick query and update per index.
- Space: O(n) for `rightMax`, the ranks and the tree.

## Pitfalls

- The comparisons are strict: an equal value on the left or right does not make a triplet, so query ranks below `r`, not up to it.
- Taking the overall largest earlier value is wrong when it is not smaller than `nums[j]`.
- The answer is at least `nums[i] + 1`, since `nums[k] > nums[j]`; starting `best` at 0 is safe.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rightMax` | largest value at or after each index |
| `rank` | position (from 1) of each distinct value in sorted order |
| `tree` | Fenwick tree: largest inserted value over a range of ranks |
| `r` | rank of `nums[j]` |
| `left`, `right` | best first and third values for middle index `j` |
| `best` | largest triplet value so far |
